subject.title: RFC 0024: Localization Runtime and Product Coverage

question: Should OpenClaw accept a shared localization kernel and product-wide coverage contract, beginning with a narrowly owner-bounded foundation, or keep localization contracts independently owned by each surface?
rationale: This RFC introduces new compatibility commitments across Gateway clients, channels, CLI/TUI rendering, plugin metadata, and release policy; a document review cannot choose that product and API direction safely.

options.title: Sponsor a scoped foundation
options.body: Accept only an owner-bounded first slice with written compatibility criteria, while deferring the remaining cross-surface contracts to follow-up decisions.

options.title: Retain surface-local localization
options.body: Do not adopt the shared runtime direction and continue to let each product surface own its existing localization workflow.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a scoped foundation
recommendation.body: Accept only an owner-bounded first slice with written compatibility criteria, while deferring the remaining cross-surface contracts to follow-up decisions.
